This asset appears under the blueprint section “TechTown Sprint 001: Style Anchor Pack” and should visibly support that gameplay or environmental role rather than acting as generic filler. The blueprint evidence is: J. Minigame support UI/assets --- 14. First build sprint Recommended first sprint is still a style anchor pack. Do not start with CyberCore Tower first. Start by proving the town reads correctly at prop scale. TechTown Sprint 001: Style Anchor Pack

Physical identity and semantic decision: the final category is furniture because dedicated family municipal_bench resolves the physical object as furniture. Model it as a human-scale furniture, fixture, workstation, storage, sanitary, or interior-use asset with credible ergonomics, supports, joinery, and a clear use case. Words describing an animal, profession, customer, owner, district, collection, or story function may not force character or creature anatomy onto an object such as a cottage, boat, crate, display, station, rack, board, feeder, machine, sign, or piece of equipment. The named object must be identifiable in neutral clay material before labels, color, and glow are applied.

Silhouette and proportion: Seat or work height, depth, back angle, leg clearance, storage volume, support placement, and reachable controls must immediately explain how a person uses the object. Keep the working envelope near 1.85 meters wide, 0.72 meters deep, and 0.9 meters high. Only reviewed protrusions such as signs, arms, doors, mirrors, roots, branches, railings, hoses, lighting, propulsion, awnings, stairs, or service hardware may extend beyond it. Every major and secondary form must reinforce Bench Futuristic; unrelated decorative mass should be removed.

Construction and functional anatomy: Model load-bearing frames, legs, pedestals, brackets, seams, cushions, panels, drawers, hinges, plumbing, glides, cable routing, fasteners, wall anchors, or floor anchors appropriate to the item. Required visible components are seat structure, back structure, side frames, supports, armrests, anchored feet. Each one must connect through credible frames, joints, seams, foundations, roots, brackets, fasteners, cables, pipes, glazing frames, hinges, biological attachment, serving structure, packaging, or material transitions. Flat paint, decals, and emission may not replace a component that explains operation, weight support, access, occupancy, growth, containment, drainage, power, preparation, protection, or maintenance.

Materials, color, and lighting: use the named material vocabulary dark brushed metal, black composite, tinted glass, controlled emissive accents, dark metal, cyan, magenta, violet, electric blue. sleek cyberpunk smart city; dark brushed metal, black composite panels, tinted glass, polished concrete, controlled cyan, magenta, violet, and electric-blue lighting. Metal surfaces need distinct painted, powder-coated, galvanized, brushed, cast, polished, oxidized, or heat-affected responses rather than one universal gray material. Glass requires thickness, framing, tint appropriate to the town, controlled transparency, believable roughness, and an interior or backing surface so it does not read as an empty blue plane. Stone, brick, concrete, plaster, stucco, tile, and asphalt should show scale-correct joints, aggregate or surface breakup, edge wear, drainage staining, and construction transitions without noisy procedural speckling. Wood needs believable board direction, grain scale, end grain, joinery, sealing, wear, and moisture response appropriate to indoor, residential, marine, fantasy, or industrial use. Fabric, upholstery, leather, rubber, and flexible polymers require thickness, seams, compression or tension cues, stitching where visible, and roughness variation tied to handling. Emissive accents must arise from a lens, strip, screen, projector, fixture, biological organ, or energy component. Do not paint unexplained neon lines across ordinary structure. Avoid the town-specific failures: Jetsons retro-future, rounded toy sci-fi, sterile white-only futurism, rainbow neon soup, Roblox block filler. Surface variation should follow manufacturing, age, handling, weather, moisture, heat, pressure, preparation, cleaning, or maintenance rather than random noise. Emissive areas must originate from a real lens, screen, fixture, projector, biological organ, or energy system.

Condition and environmental integration: Keep primary surfaces precision-made and maintained, with restrained use at handles, service fasteners, floor interfaces, vents, charging contacts, propulsion hardware, and controls. Emissive accents originate from real lenses, screens, fixtures, or energy systems and remain controlled. Place it on a named floor, wall, counter, workstation, classroom, bedroom, shop, restaurant, sanitary, storage, or service socket. Feet, wall brackets, plumbing, cable routes, backs, and user clearance must align with the room and nearby interaction positions. Add contact shadows, foundations, feet, brackets, roots, piles, seals, trim, drainage, terrain blending, waterline response, or wall transitions where the object meets its environment. It may not appear pasted into the scene or suspended by invisible support unless the design explicitly includes a justified force, mount, cable, lift field, or suspension system.

Interaction and state design: Preserve seats, drawers, doors, screens, lamps, cushions, controls, storage, plumbing fixtures, and movable surfaces as distinct objects when gameplay can sit, open, use, move, customize, or damage them. Expected hooks include seating, occupancy, or interaction sockets. Separate and name parts that can open, slide, rotate, illuminate, display content, receive an item, carry an occupant, change material, emit particles, take damage, be repaired, be harvested, or connect to another system. Static detail should remain efficient, but useful gameplay state boundaries may not be merged away.

Collision, orientation, and export: Use one or more primitive or low-complexity hulls matching the major blocking volume and interaction surface. Decorative handles, cables, slats, fasteners, trim, lenses, foliage, and surface detail must not create snagging collision. Use positive Z as the front or primary use direction and positive Y as up after export conversion. Place the origin at the ground contact, wall mount, suspension point, waterline, or logical placement center. Use one named asset root, semantically named render meshes, separate animated or stateful parts, simplified collision, and metadata for asset ID, town, family, source document, license, dimensions, final semantic category, and specification version. Remove preview cameras, lights, helpers, unused materials, duplicates, hidden placeholders, and accidental geometry before GLB export.

Performance and LOD: Keep ergonomic silhouette and contact points at every LOD. Repeated slats, legs, buttons, cushions, shelves, and fasteners should share meshes or instances. Close-range output may use up to the reviewed maximum, with a practical target near 14,040 triangles when silhouette and required components justify it. Medium-range output should target roughly 6,480 triangles while preserving primary form, supports, interaction components, openings, material blocks, and essential lights. Far output should target roughly 2,160 triangles or a suitable impostor while retaining the recognizable outline, mounting or ground relationship, and major color or emissive signature. Reduction may never destroy this recognition requirement: Seat or work height, depth, back angle, leg clearance, storage volume, support placement, and reachable controls must immediately explain how a person uses the object.

Acceptance standard: the final model must look intentional from every inspection angle, satisfy every required component, fit the reviewed scale, use meaningful material separation, remain inside geometry budgets, sit correctly on its placement plane, and export as a verified nonempty GLB. A technically valid file that looks generic, toy-like, structurally impossible, context-free, semantically misclassified, or unlike Bench Futuristic is a failure. Correct it, retry it, or quarantine it instead of publishing it.

The named object must be identifiable in neutral clay material before labels, color, and glow are applied.

Silhouette and proportion: Recognition must come from the relationship between support, enclosure, operating surface, access point, protected hardware, and ground, wall, dock, road, or network connection. Keep the working envelope near 2.8 meters wide, 5.2 meters deep, and 0.35 meters high. Only reviewed protrusions such as signs, arms, doors, mirrors, roots, branches, railings, hoses, lighting, propulsion, awnings, stairs, or service hardware may extend beyond it. Every major and secondary form must reinforce Charging Station Public; unrelated decorative mass should be removed.

Construction and functional anatomy: Include mounting, foundations or brackets, structural members, weather or pressure protection, access, hinges, latches, vents, conduit or cable paths, drainage, warnings, controls, and maintenance hardware as appropriate. Required visible components are ground pad, alignment markings, power module, connector or induction array, status lights, protective edging. Each one must connect through credible frames, joints, seams, foundations, roots, brackets, fasteners, cables, pipes, glazing frames, hinges, biological attachment, serving structure, packaging, or material transitions. Flat paint, decals, and emission may not replace a component that explains operation, weight support, access, occupancy, growth, containment, drainage, power, preparation, protection, or maintenance.

Materials, color, and lighting: use the named material vocabulary dark brushed metal, black composite, tinted glass, controlled emissive accents, dark metal, cyan, magenta, violet, electric blue. sleek cyberpunk smart city; dark brushed metal, black composite panels, tinted glass, polished concrete, controlled cyan, magenta, violet, and electric-blue lighting. Metal surfaces need distinct painted, powder-coated, galvanized, brushed, cast, polished, oxidized, or heat-affected responses rather than one universal gray material. Glass requires thickness, framing, tint appropriate to the town, controlled transparency, believable roughness, and an interior or backing surface so it does not read as an empty blue plane. Stone, brick, concrete, plaster, stucco, tile, and asphalt should show scale-correct joints, aggregate or surface breakup, edge wear, drainage staining, and construction transitions without noisy procedural speckling. Wood needs believable board direction, grain scale, end grain, joinery, sealing, wear, and moisture response appropriate to indoor, residential, marine, fantasy, or industrial use. Fabric, upholstery, leather, rubber, and flexible polymers require thickness, seams, compression or tension cues, stitching where visible, and roughness variation tied to handling. Emissive accents must arise from a lens, strip, screen, projector, fixture, biological organ, or energy component. Do not paint unexplained neon lines across ordinary structure. Avoid the town-specific failures: Jetsons retro-future, rounded toy sci-fi, sterile white-only futurism, rainbow neon soup, Roblox block filler. Surface variation should follow manufacturing, age, handling, weather, moisture, heat, pressure, preparation, cleaning, or maintenance rather than random noise. Emissive areas must originate from a real lens, screen, fixture, projector, biological organ, or energy system.

Condition and environmental integration: Keep primary surfaces precision-made and maintained, with restrained use at handles, service fasteners, floor interfaces, vents, charging contacts, propulsion hardware, and controls. Emissive accents originate from real lenses, screens, fixtures, or energy systems and remain controlled. Install it on the named ground, curb, wall, road, dock, roof, utility corridor, platform, shoreline, or service foundation. Show anchors, brackets, conduits, piles, seals, drainage, clearance, and maintenance access so the device belongs to a real network rather than floating as decoration. Add contact shadows, foundations, feet, brackets, roots, piles, seals, trim, drainage, terrain blending, waterline response, or wall transitions where the object meets its environment. It may not appear pasted into the scene or suspended by invisible support unless the design explicitly includes a justified force, mount, cable, lift field, or suspension system.

Interaction and state design: Separate controls, doors, lenses, lights, handles, hoses, nozzles, movable arms, covers, gates, scanners, cameras, and service components so systems can animate or change state. Expected hooks include day, night, powered, warning, and damaged light states. Separate and name parts that can open, slide, rotate, illuminate, display content, receive an item, carry an occupant, change material, emit particles, take damage, be repaired, be harvested, or connect to another system. Static detail should remain efficient, but useful gameplay state boundaries may not be merged away.

Collision, orientation, and export: Use one or more primitive or low-complexity hulls matching the major blocking volume and interaction surface. Decorative handles, cables, slats, fasteners, trim, lenses, foliage, and surface detail must not create snagging collision. Use positive Z as the front or primary use direction and positive Y as up after export conversion. Place the origin at the ground contact, wall mount, suspension point, waterline, or logical placement center. Use one named asset root, semantically named render meshes, separate animated or stateful parts, simplified collision, and metadata for asset ID, town, family, source document, license, dimensions, final semantic category, and specification version. Remove preview cameras, lights, helpers, unused materials, duplicates, hidden placeholders, and accidental geometry before GLB export.

Performance and LOD: Preserve functional outline, installation, and operating surfaces. Repeated bolts, louvers, bars, lenses, posts, and rails should use instancing, while collision follows major volumes. Close-range output may use up to the reviewed maximum, with a practical target near 14,040 triangles when silhouette and required components justify it. Medium-range output should target roughly 6,480 triangles while preserving primary form, supports, interaction components, openings, material blocks, and essential lights. Far output should target roughly 2,160 triangles or a suitable impostor while retaining the recognizable outline, mounting or ground relationship, and major color or emissive signature. Reduction may never destroy this recognition requirement: Recognition must come from the relationship between support, enclosure, operating surface, access point, protected hardware, and ground, wall, dock, road, or network connection.

Acceptance standard: the final model must look intentional from every inspection angle, satisfy every required component, fit the reviewed scale, use meaningful material separation, remain inside geometry budgets, sit correctly on its placement plane, and export as a verified nonempty GLB. A technically valid file that looks generic, toy-like, structurally impossible, context-free, semantically misclassified, or unlike Charging Station Public is a failure. Correct it, retry it, or quarantine it instead of publishing it.

Metal surfaces need distinct painted, powder-coated, galvanized, brushed, cast, polished, oxidized, or heat-affected responses rather than one universal gray material. Expected hooks include changeable display, content, or emissive state. Separate and name parts that can open, slide, rotate, illuminate, display content, receive an item, carry an occupant, change material, emit particles, take damage, be repaired, be harvested, or connect to another system. Static detail should remain efficient, but useful gameplay state boundaries may not be merged away.

Collision, orientation, and export: Use one or more primitive or low-complexity hulls matching the major blocking volume and interaction surface. Decorative handles, cables, slats, fasteners, trim, lenses, foliage, and surface detail must not create snagging collision. Use positive Z as the front or primary use direction and positive Y as up after export conversion. Place the origin at the ground contact, wall mount, suspension point, waterline, or logical placement center. Use one named asset root, semantically named render meshes, separate animated or stateful parts, simplified collision, and metadata for asset ID, town, family, source document, license, dimensions, final semantic category, and specification version. Remove preview cameras, lights, helpers, unused materials, duplicates, hidden placeholders, and accidental geometry before GLB export.

Performance and LOD: Preserve functional outline, installation, and operating surfaces. Repeated bolts, louvers, bars, lenses, posts, and rails should use instancing, while collision follows major volumes. Close-range output may use up to the reviewed maximum, with a practical target near 13,260 triangles when silhouette and required components justify it. Far output should target roughly 2,040 triangles or a suitable impostor while retaining the recognizable outline, mounting or ground relationship, and major color or emissive signature. Acceptance standard: the final model must look intentional from every inspection angle, satisfy every required component, fit the reviewed scale, use meaningful material separation, remain inside geometry budgets, sit correctly on its placement plane, and export as a verified nonempty GLB. Silhouette and proportion: Seat or work height, depth, back angle, leg clearance, storage volume, support placement, and reachable controls must immediately explain how a person uses the object. Keep the working envelope near 1.5 meters wide, 1.5 meters deep, and 1.5 meters high. Only reviewed protrusions such as signs, arms, doors, mirrors, roots, branches, railings, hoses, lighting, propulsion, awnings, stairs, or service hardware may extend beyond it. Every major and secondary form must reinforce Hologram Meeting Table; unrelated decorative mass should be removed.

Construction and functional anatomy: Model load-bearing frames, legs, pedestals, brackets, seams, cushions, panels, drawers, hinges, plumbing, glides, cable routing, fasteners, wall anchors, or floor anchors appropriate to the item. Required visible components are recognizable primary structure, functional secondary components, appropriate materials. Each one must connect through credible frames, joints, seams, foundations, roots, brackets, fasteners, cables, pipes, glazing frames, hinges, biological attachment, serving structure, packaging, or material transitions. Separate and name parts that can open, slide, rotate, illuminate, display content, receive an item, carry an occupant, change material, emit particles, take damage, be repaired, be harvested, or connect to another system. Decorative handles, cables, slats, fasteners, trim, lenses, foliage, and surface detail must not create snagging collision. Use positive Z as the front or primary use direction and positive Y as up after export conversion. Place the origin at the ground contact, wall mount, suspension point, waterline, or logical placement center. Use one named asset root, semantically named render meshes, separate animated or stateful parts, simplified collision, and metadata for asset ID, town, family, source document, license, dimensions, final semantic category, and specification version. Remove preview cameras, lights, helpers, unused materials, duplicates, hidden placeholders, and accidental geometry before GLB export.

Performance and LOD: Keep ergonomic silhouette and contact points at every LOD. Repeated slats, legs, buttons, cushions, shelves, and fasteners should share meshes or instances. Close-range output may use up to the reviewed maximum, with a practical target near 23,400 triangles when silhouette and required components justify it. Medium-range output should target roughly 10,800 triangles while preserving primary form, supports, interaction components, openings, material blocks, and essential lights. Far output should target roughly 3,600 triangles or a suitable impostor while retaining the recognizable outline, mounting or ground relationship, and major color or emissive signature. Acceptance standard: the final model must look intentional from every inspection angle, satisfy every required component, fit the reviewed scale, use meaningful material separation, remain inside geometry budgets, sit correctly on its placement plane, and export as a verified nonempty GLB. Separate and name parts that can open, slide, rotate, illuminate, display content, receive an item, carry an occupant, change material, emit particles, take damage, be repaired, be harvested, or connect to another system. Place the origin at the ground, waterline, rail, or hover-plane center below the chassis or hull, with separate transforms for propulsion and steering hardware. Respect adult seating dimensions, back angle, load-bearing frames, fasteners, and ground anchors. The object must remain immediately recognizable from silhouette and required components, use physically coherent construction and human or vehicle scale, and follow the town direction: sleek cyberpunk smart city; dark brushed metal, black composite panels, tinted glass, polished concrete, controlled cyan, magenta, violet, and electric-blue lighting. This asset appears under the blueprint section “F. Electronics / drone / gadget retail” and should visibly support that gameplay or environmental role rather than acting as generic filler. The blueprint evidence is: E. Food / restaurant / convenience F. Electronics / drone / gadget retail

Physical identity and semantic decision: the final category is furniture because dedicated family municipal_bench resolves the physical object as furniture. Model it as a human-scale furniture, fixture, workstation, storage, sanitary, or interior-use asset with credible ergonomics, supports, joinery, and a clear use case. Words describing an animal, profession, customer, owner, district, collection, or story function may not force character or creature anatomy onto an object such as a cottage, boat, crate, display, station, rack, board, feeder, machine, sign, or piece of equipment. The named object must be identifiable in neutral clay material before labels, color, and glow are applied.

Silhouette and proportion: Seat or work height, depth, back angle, leg clearance, storage volume, support placement, and reachable controls must immediately explain how a person uses the object. Keep the working envelope near 1.85 meters wide, 0.72 meters deep, and 0.9 meters high. Only reviewed protrusions such as signs, arms, doors, mirrors, roots, branches, railings, hoses, lighting, propulsion, awnings, stairs, or service hardware may extend beyond it. Every major and secondary form must reinforce Tool Bench Precision; unrelated decorative mass should be removed.

Construction and functional anatomy: Model load-bearing frames, legs, pedestals, brackets, seams, cushions, panels, drawers, hinges, plumbing, glides, cable routing, fasteners, wall anchors, or floor anchors appropriate to the item. Required visible components are seat structure, back structure, side frames, supports, armrests, anchored feet. Each one must connect through credible frames, joints, seams, foundations, roots, brackets, fasteners, cables, pipes, glazing frames, hinges, biological attachment, serving structure, packaging, or material transitions. Flat paint, decals, and emission may not replace a component that explains operation, weight support, access, occupancy, growth, containment, drainage, power, preparation, protection, or maintenance.

Materials, color, and lighting: use the named material vocabulary dark brushed metal, black composite, tinted glass, controlled emissive accents, dark metal, cyan, magenta, violet, electric blue. sleek cyberpunk smart city; dark brushed metal, black composite panels, tinted glass, polished concrete, controlled cyan, magenta, violet, and electric-blue lighting. Metal surfaces need distinct painted, powder-coated, galvanized, brushed, cast, polished, oxidized, or heat-affected responses rather than one universal gray material. Glass requires thickness, framing, tint appropriate to the town, controlled transparency, believable roughness, and an interior or backing surface so it does not read as an empty blue plane. Stone, brick, concrete, plaster, stucco, tile, and asphalt should show scale-correct joints, aggregate or surface breakup, edge wear, drainage staining, and construction transitions without noisy procedural speckling. Wood needs believable board direction, grain scale, end grain, joinery, sealing, wear, and moisture response appropriate to indoor, residential, marine, fantasy, or industrial use. Fabric, upholstery, leather, rubber, and flexible polymers require thickness, seams, compression or tension cues, stitching where visible, and roughness variation tied to handling. Emissive accents must arise from a lens, strip, screen, projector, fixture, biological organ, or energy component. Do not paint unexplained neon lines across ordinary structure. Avoid the town-specific failures: Jetsons retro-future, rounded toy sci-fi, sterile white-only futurism, rainbow neon soup, Roblox block filler. Surface variation should follow manufacturing, age, handling, weather, moisture, heat, pressure, preparation, cleaning, or maintenance rather than random noise. Emissive areas must originate from a real lens, screen, fixture, projector, biological organ, or energy system.

Condition and environmental integration: Keep primary surfaces precision-made and maintained, with restrained use at handles, service fasteners, floor interfaces, vents, charging contacts, propulsion hardware, and controls. Emissive accents originate from real lenses, screens, fixtures, or energy systems and remain controlled. Place it on a named floor, wall, counter, workstation, classroom, bedroom, shop, restaurant, sanitary, storage, or service socket. Feet, wall brackets, plumbing, cable routes, backs, and user clearance must align with the room and nearby interaction positions. Add contact shadows, foundations, feet, brackets, roots, piles, seals, trim, drainage, terrain blending, waterline response, or wall transitions where the object meets its environment. It may not appear pasted into the scene or suspended by invisible support unless the design explicitly includes a justified force, mount, cable, lift field, or suspension system.

Interaction and state design: Preserve seats, drawers, doors, screens, lamps, cushions, controls, storage, plumbing fixtures, and movable surfaces as distinct objects when gameplay can sit, open, use, move, customize, or damage them. Expected hooks include seating, occupancy, or interaction sockets. Separate and name parts that can open, slide, rotate, illuminate, display content, receive an item, carry an occupant, change material, emit particles, take damage, be repaired, be harvested, or connect to another system. Static detail should remain efficient, but useful gameplay state boundaries may not be merged away.

Collision, orientation, and export: Use one or more primitive or low-complexity hulls matching the major blocking volume and interaction surface. Decorative handles, cables, slats, fasteners, trim, lenses, foliage, and surface detail must not create snagging collision. Use positive Z as the front or primary use direction and positive Y as up after export conversion. Place the origin at the ground contact, wall mount, suspension point, waterline, or logical placement center. Use one named asset root, semantically named render meshes, separate animated or stateful parts, simplified collision, and metadata for asset ID, town, family, source document, license, dimensions, final semantic category, and specification version. Remove preview cameras, lights, helpers, unused materials, duplicates, hidden placeholders, and accidental geometry before GLB export.

Performance and LOD: Keep ergonomic silhouette and contact points at every LOD. Repeated slats, legs, buttons, cushions, shelves, and fasteners should share meshes or instances. Close-range output may use up to the reviewed maximum, with a practical target near 14,040 triangles when silhouette and required components justify it. Medium-range output should target roughly 6,480 triangles while preserving primary form, supports, interaction components, openings, material blocks, and essential lights. Far output should target roughly 2,160 triangles or a suitable impostor while retaining the recognizable outline, mounting or ground relationship, and major color or emissive signature. Reduction may never destroy this recognition requirement: Seat or work height, depth, back angle, leg clearance, storage volume, support placement, and reachable controls must immediately explain how a person uses the object.

Acceptance standard: the final model must look intentional from every inspection angle, satisfy every required component, fit the reviewed scale, use meaningful material separation, remain inside geometry budgets, sit correctly on its placement plane, and export as a verified nonempty GLB. A technically valid file that looks generic, toy-like, structurally impossible, context-free, semantically misclassified, or unlike Tool Bench Precision is a failure. Correct it, retry it, or quarantine it instead of publishing it.
